issues.description: Return type of messageOnMilk() is inconsistent: the problem statement (UML and textual description) and the template Main expect messageOnMilk() to return a String (the textual message to be printed), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return boolean and the implementations (Seal, Goat) print the message and return true. This mismatch prevents students from implementing the intended API (a method that returns the milk message String) and will confuse tests or Main code that assume a String return value.
issues.suggestedFix: Make Milkable.messageOnMilk() return String to match the UML and textual specification. Update the Milkable interface signature to 'String messageOnMilk();' and change implementations (Seal, Goat) to return the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" instead of printing and returning boolean. Ensure Main and tests print or assert the returned String.

issues.description: The problem statement defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning a String and describes that it should return the message "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (and the template/Main uses System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk()) expecting a printable message). In the solution repository, the Milkable interface and its implementations use a boolean return type: Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns boolean and Goat/Seal implementations print the message internally and return true. This mismatch in the method contract (expected String vs. implemented boolean) breaks the conceptual mapping for students: they are told to implement and use a method that returns a String message, but the solution provides a method with the same name that returns a boolean and has different behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable contract with the problem statement: change the interface signature to 'String messageOnMilk();' and update Goat and Seal to return the message string (e.g., return "Goat " + getName() + " is milked"). Remove internal printing from the implementations so callers (like Main) can print the returned String with System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk()).
